# Design Document — verification-loop

## Overview

This design adds a merge fix round for the run's own blocked PR, a per-step implementer model route, a security pass in the completion gate, and a new-dependency flag on every PR read. It changes the merge stage (`src/controller/merge.ts`, `src/controller/runs.ts`), the implementation phase (`src/controller/phases/implementation.ts`), the brief templates and the Run page PR panel. It reuses the step runner, `harness gate class-a`, the existing brief templates, the run ledger and the deferral store.

## Steering Document Alignment

### Technical Standards (tech.md)
N/A: the steering directory holds no `tech.md`; the design follows `agent-rules.md` (tests next to the module, node 20 fields only, `gh` and `claude` through the stubs).

### Project Structure (structure.md)
N/A: no `structure.md`. New controller modules go in `src/controller/`, their tests in the `__tests__/` directory next to them, as `agent-rules.md` "Layout" states.

### Design System (design-system.md) — if applicable
N/A: no `design-system.md`. The new chip reuses the PR panel's chip classes and CSS variables (`src/dashboard_frontend/src/modules/shell/RunPage.tsx:332-337`), so both themes stay in step.

## Architecture

The merge rule stays code and gains two read-only outputs: a kind per blocking reason and the new dependencies. The run loop decides on a fix round and starts it through a new module. The implementation phase gains a model route per implementer step and a security stage before the HANDOFF write. Every count and resume point is a ledger `note`, read back by pure functions.

```mermaid
graph LR
    MR[mergeByRule - code only] -->|blocked + kinds| RL[runMergeStageStep]
    MR -->|newDependencies| PR[PrRead on run record]
    PR --> UI[Run page PR panel]
    RL -->|eligible| MF[runMergeFixRound - sdd-implementer]
    MF -->|push or rerun, then merging| RL
    RL -->|cap reached or other kind| EW[error wait]
    CG[completionGate] --> E2E[e2e verifier]
    E2E -->|pass note| SP[security pass - sdd-verifier]
    SP -->|findings| SF[security fix rounds, adjudicator]
    SP -->|suspicions| DF[deferrals owner matthew]
    SF -->|still open| SW[escalation wait]
    SP -->|clean or accepted| HO[HANDOFF, push, PR]
```

## Components and Interfaces

### C1 — Blocking kinds and PR facts in the merge evaluation (R1 AC 1, AC 11; R4 AC 1)
- **Interfaces:**
  - `export type BlockingKind = 'check' | 'conflict' | 'trailer' | 'head' | 'other'`.
  - `export interface BlockingReason { kind: BlockingKind; text: string; check?: { name: string; runId?: number } }`; `text` equals the string pushed onto `reasons`.
  - `MergeEvaluation.blocking?: BlockingReason[]`: set only when `ready` is false and neither `pending` nor `unreadable` is set. A ready result stays exactly `{ ready: true, reasons: [] }`.
  - `PullRequestEvaluation.head?: string` (`headRefOid`) and `base?: string` (`baseRefName`).
  - `MergeStageResult.blocking?` and `MergeStageResult.base?`, copied from the evaluation on a `blocked` return.
- **Post-conditions:** a failed workflow run gives `check` with `name` and `runId` (`Number(r.id)`); a failed commit status gives `check` with no `runId`; `mergeable === 'CONFLICTING'` gives `conflict`; any other value that is not `MERGEABLE` or `UNKNOWN` gives `other`; a head branch mismatch gives `head`; an attribution trailer gives `trailer`. Pending reasons get no entry. The kind comes from the branch that pushed the reason (`src/controller/merge.ts:357-405`), never from its text.
- **Dependencies:** `PR_VIEW_FIELDS` gains `baseRefName` (`src/controller/merge.ts:38-39`); probe: `gh pr view --json` on the installed gh 2.95.0 lists it. No new `gh` call. Changes land in `evaluatePullRequest` (`src/controller/merge.ts:319-412`) and `mergeByRule` (`:568-642`).

### C2 — New-dependency reader (R4 AC 1-3, AC 5-7)
- **Interfaces** (new file `src/controller/new-deps.ts`):
  - `export const DEPENDENCY_SECTIONS = ['dependencies', 'devDependencies', 'peerDependencies', 'optionalDependencies'] as const`.
  - `export function diffNewDependencies(before: unknown, after: unknown): string[]`: pure; the union of names over the four sections of `after` minus the union over `before`, sorted and unique. A missing or non-object side counts as empty.
  - `export function readNewDependencies(repoDir: string, baseBranch: string, head: string): { ok: true; names: string[] } | { ok: false; reason: string }`: resolve the base as `origin/<baseBranch>`, else `<baseBranch>`, and the head, with `git rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}`; take `git merge-base`; list `git diff --name-only --no-renames <mergeBase> <head>`; keep paths whose basename is `package.json`; read both sides with `git show <rev>:<path>` (a missing base side is empty); return the union of `diffNewDependencies` per file. A failed git call or a head manifest that does not parse gives `ok: false` with one line of why. Never throws.
- **Wiring in `mergeByRule`:** when the evaluation is not `unreadable` and has `head` and `base`, call `readNewDependencies(pr.repoDir, base, head)`. A non-empty list goes on the `PrRead` as `newDependencies`; an empty one leaves the field absent. The list never changes `ready`, `reasons`, `blocking`, the status or a wait (R4 AC 7).
- **Ledger:** `MergeStageDeps.ledger` widens to `Pick<RunLedger, 'prMerged' | 'note' | 'path'>`. The pass reads this run's rows from `deps.ledger.path`, takes the newest note that starts `new dependencies: <repo>#<n>:`, and writes a note only when the new text differs (Data Models). No prior note and an empty list write nothing.
- **Dependencies:** git through `execFileSync` with `scrubbedGitEnv()`, as `src/controller/merge.ts:459-465` does; tests read only `stdout`, which node 20 guarantees.

### C3 — Merge fix round (R1 AC 1-10)
- **Interfaces** (new file `src/controller/merge-fix.ts`):
  - `export const MERGE_FIX_CAP = 2`.
  - `export function mergeFixHistory(rows: Record<string, string>[], runId: string): { used: number; endings: string[] }`: pure; reads this run's `merge fix round <k> end:` notes. `used` counts every end note except the ending `step usage-limit`.
  - `export function mergeFixEligible(result: MergeStageResult, used: number): boolean`: pure; true when `blocked`, `blocking` is non-empty and all `check` or `conflict`, and `used < MERGE_FIX_CAP`.
  - `export async function runMergeFixRound(ctx: MergeFixContext, input: { round: number; pr: number; blocking: BlockingReason[]; base: string }): Promise<MergeFixOutcome>`. `MergeFixContext` holds `run`, `worktree`, `specStoreRoot`, `specDir`, `ledger`, `stepLogDir`, `mcpConfig`, the four step callbacks of `ImplementationPhaseContext`, and an optional trailing `scratchDir` (default `/tmp/scratchpad/sdd/<spec>`). `MergeFixOutcome` is `{ kind: 'pushed' | 'rechecked' | 'ended' | 'usage-limit'; ending: string }`.
- **Post-conditions of `runMergeFixRound`, in order:**
  1. Note `merge fix round <k> start: <blocking texts joined by "; ">` (R1 AC 10).
  2. Worktree branch is not `run.branch`: ending `not on the PR branch`, no spawn.
  3. `impl-standing.md` re-written through the `brief` action with the values of `src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:469-474`.
  4. Per `check` with a `runId`: `gh run view <id> --log-failed`, last 80 lines saved as `merge-ci-<name>-r<k>.log` in the scratch dir, as `src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:1117-1126` does.
  5. Brief: template `fix`, variant `merge` (C4).
  6. One step on `sdd-implementer` at the profile model and effort (R2 AC 10), in `worktree`, with `IMPLEMENTER_SCHEMA`, and the three spawn rows `runModelStep` writes (`src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:371-418`), label `merge fix round <k>`.
  7. The ending, written as `merge fix round <k> end: <ending>`: a step that is not `ok` gives `step <classification>` (kind `usage-limit` for a usage limit, else `ended`); `INFRA:` runs `gh run rerun <id> --failed` per run id and gives `infra: <line>`, kind `rechecked` (R1 AC 5); `DESIGN-DEFECT:` or `ESCALATE:` gives `design-defect: <line>` or `escalate: <line>`, kind `ended` (R1 AC 6); an unchanged HEAD gives `no commit`; a HEAD whose ancestors do not include the old HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) gives `history rewritten; not pushed` (R1 AC 3); else `git push origin HEAD`, never `--force`, gives `pushed <sha7>`, kind `pushed`, or `push failed: <line>`, kind `ended` (R1 AC 4).
- **Wiring in `runMergeStageStep`, case `blocked`** (`src/controller/runs.ts:669-682`): read the rows, `mergeFixHistory`, `mergeFixEligible`. When eligible, check `deps.isCancelled`, the token cap and `deps.windowBlock()` first, because the merge resume path runs before those checks in `runOnce` (`src/controller/runs.ts:746-778`); a blocked window pauses with no round. Then run the round. `usage-limit` pauses the run as `usage-limit`; every other kind saves status `merging` with `resumeAt: nextMergeCheck(deps)` and returns `stop`, so the next pass reads the new state (R1 AC 4-6). When not eligible: the `error` wait as today, and when `used > 0` its text adds `<used> fix round(s) ran: round 1 <ending>; round 2 <ending>.` (R1 AC 7). `runCloseoutMergeStep` does not change (R1 AC 12). A "retry" re-enters through the existing `merge` cursor and reads the same count (R1 AC 9).
- **Reuses:** `runStep` and `loadRole` (`src/controller/step.ts:229-242`, `:343-358`), the `brief` action, `stepLifecycle` and `stepActivityForwarder` (`src/controller/runs.ts:425-449`).

### C4 — Brief variants (R1 AC 2-3, R3 AC 3-7)
- **Interfaces** (`src/tools/brief-templates.ts`):
  - `renderFix` (`src/tools/brief-templates.ts:713-750`) sends variant `merge` to a new `renderMergeFix` and variant `security` to a new `renderSecurityFix`. The `fix` template's required keys stay (`src/tools/brief-templates.ts:1553-1557`); callers pass `taskId` `merge` or `security` and `commit: 'none'`.
  - `renderMergeFix(v)`: heading `# PR #<pr> — merge fix round <round> (spec <spec>)`; the `impl-standing.md` read-and-obey line; for checks, their names, log paths and the reproduce-first text of `renderCiFix` (`src/tools/brief-templates.ts:682-705`); for a conflict, "the branch conflicts with `<base>`: run `git fetch origin <base>`, then `git merge origin/<base>`, resolve, run the checks, commit the merge"; always "never rebase, never amend a pushed commit, never push: the controller pushes"; the `INFRA:` paragraph; the implementer report block.
  - `renderSecurityFix(v)`: the findings; "make each command stop reproducing, add coverage that fails without the fix, commit, do not push"; the report block.
  - `renderVerifier` (`src/tools/brief-templates.ts:833-848`) sends variants `security` and `security-narrow` to a new `renderVerifierSecurity`; callers fill the other required keys with empty strings, as `src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:961-963` does.
  - `renderVerifierSecurity(v)` takes `base`, `sensitiveFiles`, `otherFiles`, `scratch` and, for the narrow variant, `findings`. It scopes the review to `git diff <base>...HEAD` with the sensitive files listed first (R3 AC 3); it says to write reproductions only under `<scratch>/security/` (NFR Security); it says a finding carries the exact command and the output it produced, and anything not reproduced is a suspicion with one line of why (R3 AC 4). The narrow variant says to re-run only the listed findings' commands and report only those that still reproduce (R3 AC 6).

### C5 — Implementer model route (R2)
- **Interfaces** (new file `src/controller/implementer-route.ts`):
  - `export interface ImplementerRoute { model: string; effort: string; reason: string }`.
  - `export function routeForTask(items: { taskId: string; kind: string; reason: string }[] | null, taskId: string): ImplementerRoute`. The first `sensitive-path` item for the task gives the `sdd-implementer` profile and the item's `reason`. None gives the `sdd-test-author` profile's model and effort (`harness/agent-profiles.json:50-55`) and `no sensitive-path flag`. `null` (the class-a call failed) gives the `sdd-implementer` profile and `class-a unavailable`. `keyword` items are ignored (R2 AC 3). Both profiles come from `loadRole` (`src/controller/step.ts:229-242`).
- **Wiring in `runImplementationPhase`:**
  - A closure `classAItems()` calls `harnessHandler({ action: 'gate', op: 'class-a', specName }, toolContext)`, the call of `src/controller/phases/gates.ts:291-294`, and returns `items`, or `null` on failure. It runs at every task step start, so the flag reads the `tasks.md` and `## Sensitive paths` current then (R2 AC 4). With no list `computeClassA` gives no path item (`src/core/veto-rules.ts:65-101`), so every task takes the test author profile (R2 AC 5).
  - `runModelStep` gains an optional trailing option `model?: { model: string; effort: string }`. When set it fills `StepSpec.model` and `StepSpec.effort` (`src/controller/step.ts:108-111`) and replaces `loadRole(role)`'s values in the `spawn.start` model and effort and the `spawn.end` model (R2 AC 8).
  - The task steps pass it: the implement attempts (`src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:629-634`), the checks-file re-spawn (`:658-661`) and the task fix rounds (`:774-778`). The repair round (`:994-997`), the reconcile round (`:1137-1140`), the merge fix round and the security fix round do not (R2 AC 10); nor do the test author, verifier and adjudicator (R2 AC 11).
  - The note `task <id> route <model> <effort>: <reason>` is written at the task's first step start (R2 AC 9); a later step of the task whose route differs from the newest route note writes one more. The model is fixed in the `StepSpec` at the spawn and no implementer step is passed `--resume`, so a step never changes model (R2 AC 6).

### C6 — Completion gate: e2e record and security pass (R3)
- **Interfaces** (new file `src/controller/phases/security-pass.ts`, pure):
  - `export interface SecurityFinding { title: string; file: string; command: string; output: string }`; `export interface SecuritySuspicion { title: string; file: string; why: string }`.
  - `export const SECURITY_SCHEMA`: `findings` (array of the four finding fields), `suspicions` (array of the three suspicion fields), `retro`; `additionalProperties: true`.
  - `export function classifySecurityReport(report: unknown): { findings: SecurityFinding[]; suspicions: SecuritySuspicion[] }`: a finding with an empty `command` or `output` becomes a suspicion with why `reported without a reproduction` (R3 AC 5); `output` is cut to 400 characters.
  - `export function e2ePassStands(rows): boolean`: true when the newer of the notes `e2e verification passed` and `completion handoff written` is the first.
  - `export function readSecurityState(rows): SecurityState`, `SecurityState = { epoch: number; next: 'pass' | 'fix' | 'recheck' | 'adjudicate' | 'recheck-adjudicated' | 'escalate' | 'await-answer' | 'done'; fixRounds: number; open: SecurityFinding[]; accepted: SecurityFinding[]; answered: string[] }`, from the `security:` notes after the newest `security: epoch` note; `answered` and `accepted` read the whole run. `next` follows the last stage note: none gives `pass`; `pass` or a recheck with no open finding gives `done`, with open findings `fix` while `fixRounds` is under 2, then `adjudicate`, and after `recheck adjudicated` `escalate`; `fix round` gives `recheck`; `adjudicator` gives `recheck-adjudicated`; `escalated` gives `await-answer`; `done` gives `done`.
  - `export function suspicionKey(s: SecuritySuspicion): string`: the first 8 hex characters of `sha1(file + '|' + title)`.
- **Flow in `completionGate`** (`src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:879-956`):
  1. `e2ePassStands(rows)`: skip the e2e loop (R3 AC 13). Else run it as today and write `e2e verification passed` on the pass.
  2. Sensitive = `classAItems()` holds a `sensitive-path` item, or returned `null`. Not sensitive: no security step and no `security:` row (R3 AC 2).
  3. Sensitive: loop on `readSecurityState` until `done` or a stop, checking `ctx.shouldStop` before each step:
     - no epoch note: write `security: epoch 1`;
     - `pass`: the `security` verifier step on `sdd-verifier` (R3 AC 1). Base = `git merge-base HEAD <default>`, the default being `origin/HEAD`'s target, else `main`, else `master`; with none, the first `task <id> pick head` note. File lists from `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD`, split by `isSensitivePath` (`src/core/gate-rules.ts:158-160`) (R3 AC 3);
     - `fix`: the `security` fix round on `sdd-implementer` at the profile model, no push (R3 AC 6);
     - `recheck`, `recheck-adjudicated`: the `security-narrow` verifier step over `open`;
     - `adjudicate`: template `adjudicator`, `taskId: 'security'`, `items` = the open findings (R3 AC 7);
     - `escalate`: write `security: escalated`, return `{ result: 'security-open', findings: open }` (R3 AC 8);
     - `await-answer`: take the oldest `ctx.securityAnswers` entry whose `waitId` is not in `answered`; none returns `security-open` again. `accept` writes `security: answer <waitId> accept`, `security: accepted <json>`, one retro entry per finding (category `ruling`), then `security: done`. `retry` writes `security: answer <waitId> retry` and `security: epoch <n+1>` and loops with no e2e step (R3 AC 9).
     After each verifier step and fix round, write its counts note and `security: open <json>` (R3 AC 12). For each suspicion whose key has no `security: suspicion <key> deferral` note, create one deferral (owner `matthew`, tags `['security']`, `originSpec`, `originPhase: 'implementation'`, `body.context` = `<file>: <why>`) and write that note with its id (R3 AC 10-11).
  4. At `done`, each accepted finding goes into `gotchas` as `accepted security finding: <title> (<file>)` and into the PR body's Test plan (`buildPrBody`, `src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:1042-1057`) as `- [ ] accepted security finding: <title> (<file>): <command>` (R3 AC 9).
  5. The HANDOFF write as today, then the note `completion handoff written`.
- **Phase interfaces:** `ImplementationPhaseOutcome.result` gains `'security-open'` and an optional `findings?: SecurityFinding[]`; `ImplementationPhaseContext` gains an optional `securityAnswers?: { waitId: string; value: string }[]`, oldest first.
- **Reuses:** `DeferralStorage.create` (`src/core/deferral-storage.ts:229-232`; `owner` is a record field, `src/types.ts:310-328`).

### C7 — Security escalation wait (R3 AC 8-9)
- `handleImplementationOutcome` (`src/controller/runs.ts:1015-1056`) maps `security-open` to an `escalation` wait with one question `{ id: 'security', text, options: ['accept', 'retry', 'abandon'] }` and no `recommended`; `text` lists each open finding as `<title> (<file>): <command>`. When an open escalation wait with question id `security` exists for the run, it parks the run without a second wait.
- A new `securityAnswers(runId)` returns the answered escalation waits with question id `security`, oldest first, as `{ waitId, value }`; `runOnce` passes it to `runImplementationPhase` (`src/controller/runs.ts:859-867`).
- `escalationRulings` (`src/controller/runs.ts:997-1008`) skips waits with question id `security`, so `accept` never reaches a brief as a ruling.
- `abandon` takes the existing path: the controller cancels a run whose escalation wait is answered `abandon` (`src/controller/controller.ts:353-358`), so the gate never reaches the HANDOFF write or the push.

### C8 — Run page dependency chip (R4 AC 3-4)
- `PrRead.newDependencies?: string[]` (`src/controller/state.ts:109-126`), and the same optional field on both hand copies (`src/dashboard/shell/types.ts:161-172`, `src/dashboard_frontend/src/modules/shell/types.ts:184-195`). `toRow` passes `prReads` as is (`src/controller/runs.ts:1227-1235`).
- `PrPanel` (`src/dashboard_frontend/src/modules/shell/RunPage.tsx:345-394`), when the field is non-empty, renders a chip `new dependency` with the `pending` chip classes (`src/dashboard_frontend/src/modules/shell/RunPage.tsx:332-337`) and `data-testid` `pr-deps-<repo>-<number>`, then the names joined by ", ".

### C9 — Documentation (R5)
- `docs/adr/0003-merge-by-rule.md` gets an amendment dated the day the task lands: a `blocked` run PR whose every blocking reason is a red check or a conflict gets up to 2 implementer fix rounds before the `error` wait; the merge rule stays code.
- `docs/controller-design.md` section 10 (`:194-208`) gets one paragraph: the fix rounds, the new-dependency flag, and that neither changes the merge verdict.

## Data Models

Ledger notes, the resume contract (each is a `note` row with this `text`):
```
merge fix round <k> start: <reason>; <reason>
merge fix round <k> end: <ending>     # pushed <sha7> | push failed: … | infra: … | design-defect: … | escalate: … | no commit | not on the PR branch | history rewritten; not pushed | step <classification>
new dependencies: <repo>#<n>: <a, b> | none | unreadable (<why>)
task <id> route <model> <effort>: <reason>
e2e verification passed
completion handoff written
security: epoch <n>
security: pass: findings <f>, suspicions <s>
security: fix round <k>: findings <f>, suspicions 0
security: recheck <k>: findings <f>, suspicions <s>
security: adjudicator: findings <f>, suspicions 0
security: recheck adjudicated: findings <f>, suspicions <s>
security: open <json SecurityFinding[]>
security: suspicion <key> deferral <id>
security: escalated
security: answer <waitId> <accept|retry>
security: accepted <json SecurityFinding[]>
security: done
```
`none` follows only a logged non-empty list. Type shapes are in C1, C2, C6 and C8; inline samples are illustrative — verify against the test fake.

## Error Handling

1. **Class-a call fails:** strict path (D7); the route note says `class-a unavailable`.
2. **Merge fix push fails, history rewritten, or worktree off the branch:** no push; the round counts, so the cap ends the loop at the `error` wait.
3. **Dependency read fails:** no list, one note per change of state, verdict untouched (R4 AC 6).
4. **Security step not `ok`:** the phase returns `error` as other steps do (`src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:414-416`); the notes so far resume the loop at that step.
5. **Security report with no structured output:** empty lists, so the pass ends `done` with a zero counts note in the ledger.

## Testing Strategy

- **Unit:**
  - New `src/controller/__tests__/new-deps.test.ts`: `diffNewDependencies` for an added, moved, re-versioned and removed name and a new manifest; `readNewDependencies` on a temp git repo (one added dependency, a lockfile-only commit, a missing sha).
  - New `src/controller/__tests__/merge-fix.test.ts`: `mergeFixEligible` for each kind mix at `used` 0, 1, 2; `mergeFixHistory` over two runs' rows and a `step usage-limit` ending; `runMergeFixRound` with `scripts/stub-claude.mjs` `commands` against a bare remote (pushed), with no commit, with a rewritten HEAD (not pushed), and with `INFRA:` (the `gh run rerun` argv `scripts/stub-gh.mjs` records); the brief names the log path and, for a conflict, the merge instruction.
  - New `src/controller/__tests__/implementer-route.test.ts`: a sensitive item, keyword-only items, no items, `null`.
  - New `src/controller/phases/__tests__/security-pass.test.ts`: `classifySecurityReport`, `e2ePassStands`, `readSecurityState` for each `next` value, two epochs, an answered wait id.
  - `src/controller/__tests__/merge.test.ts`: the six kinds; `base` and `head`; `newDependencies` and the note dedupe over two passes; the unreadable note once. The exact `{ ready: true, reasons: [] }` assertions (`:172`, `:255`) and the `gh` argv counts (`:471`, `:486`, `:497`) keep their values.
  - `src/tools/__tests__/harness.test.ts`: the four new variants render the lines C4 pins.
  - `src/__tests__/agent-profiles.test.ts` stays green with no edit.
- **Integration:**
  - `src/controller/__tests__/runs.test.ts`: a blocked red check runs one round and leaves the run `merging` with a `resumeAt`; after two rounds the `error` wait names both endings; a trailer, a "retry" after the cap, and a blocked close-out PR (R1 AC 12, verified) each open the `error` wait with no spawn; `security-open` opens one escalation wait with three options.
  - `src/controller/phases/__tests__/implementation.test.ts`: the stub init event's `argv` has `--model claude-sonnet-5` for an unflagged task and `--model claude-opus-4-8` for a sensitive one, and the spawn rows match; repair and reconcile keep the profile; one route note per task; a re-entry after the e2e note spawns no e2e verifier; the security loop through fix, recheck, adjudicator and `security-open`; one deferral per suspicion across re-entries; `accept` reaches the Gotchas row, the PR body and the retro log; `retry` writes epoch 2.
  - `e2e/worktree-shell.spec.ts`: the seeded run record (`:163-170`) gains `newDependencies` on one read; assert the `pr-deps-` chip and names. The task that edits `RunPage.tsx` names this suite.
- **End-to-end:** the entry has no scenario beyond Delivers; the verifier checks its four items through the integration tests, then runs `npm run build` and `npm test`.

## Decisions taken in this document

- D1 — Kinds go in a separate blocking list: options were a parallel kinds array, objects in place of reason strings, or a separate list; chosen because the reason strings stay unchanged on the wire and in tests.
- D2 — The fix round is a new module the run loop calls: options were the merge rule, the phase closure, or a new module; chosen because the merge rule stays model-free and the closure is unreachable from the merge stage.
- D3 — A round counts at its end note, except a usage-limit ending: options were start notes, end notes, or spawn rows; chosen because an interrupted round should run again.
- D4 — Every round ends with the run in merging and a re-check time: options were an immediate re-pass or the scheduler; chosen because one path is simpler.
- D5 — The controller pushes only after an ancestry check: options were trusting the brief or checking in code; chosen because code then enforces the no-rewrite rule.
- D6 — The route is computed at every task step start: options were a pin at pick or per step; chosen because the requirement names the task file current at the step start.
- D7 — A failed class-a call takes the strict path for both routing and the security pass: options were the cheap or the strict path; chosen because a missed sensitive flag costs more than one extra step.
- D8 — The e2e pass stands until the next HANDOFF marker: options were a run-wide flag or a marker-bounded one; chosen because a re-entry after the HANDOFF write must behave as today.
- D9 — Security loop state is ledger notes, open findings as JSON: options were a scratch file, a spec-store file, or notes; chosen because scratch may vanish and counts must come from the ledger.
- D10 — The security wait recommends nothing: options were accept, retry, or none; chosen because the findings survived the whole loop and the call is the operator's.
- D11 — Abandon reuses the existing escalation cancel: options were a new stopped state or the cancel; chosen because it gives no HANDOFF write and no push with no new status.
- D12 — Each security answer applies once, by wait id: options were the newest wait only or tracked ids; chosen because two epochs can each end in a wait.
- D13 — The security diff base is the merge base with the default branch, else the first task pick head: options were the PR base, the default branch, or the pick head; chosen because no PR exists yet.
- D14 — No base or head in the view skips the dependency read with no note: options were a note or a skip; chosen because a readable view always has both and the test views carry no base.
